articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infections are rapidly expanding; infectiousness is about 10 times that of influenza; vaccination is effective for prevention: Chunichi Shimbun Web.
articles.summary: Measles infections are rapidly expanding in Japan, with 362 cases reported as of April 19, 2026—the second fastest pace in a decade. In the Chubu region's nine prefectures, Aichi prefecture experienced a cluster, while Tokyo leads nationwide and Kagoshima also reports a cluster. The measles virus is highly infectious, estimated to spread to 12–18 people from a single case in susceptible groups; household transmission can reach ~90%. Incubation is 10–12 days, followed by high fever and rash; pneumonia or encephalitis can occur, with infants and pregnant women at higher risk. About 70% of cases are aged 10–30s. Two-dose vaccination is protective; 2024–2025 coverage was 91% vs a 95% target. Many adults in their 30s–50s have only one dose; MR vaccination is available at roughly 10,000–15,000 yen. Post-exposure vaccination within 72 hours can prevent disease; during holidays avoid public transport if symptomatic and ensure pre-travel vaccination for outbreak areas.

articles.summary: Measles cases in Saitama Prefecture have surged to 29 this year as of April 28, about double last year’s 13, and nearing the 2019 peak of 35. Over the past decade, cases have climbed, with 27 patients reported by April 26 across age groups: under 10 (1), teens (4), 20s (8), 30s–40s (5 each), and 50s (4). Nationally, 362 cases were recorded by April 19, more than fourfold the 83 reported at the same time last year; Tokyo leads with 153, followed by Kanagawa (36) and Kagoshima (34). Measles is highly contagious, transmitting via droplets, contact, and airborne routes; incubation is 10–12 days, followed by cold-like symptoms, fever above 39°C, and rash, with pneumonia or encephalitis possible as complications. Prevention emphasizes ventilation and two-dose vaccination; suspected cases should contact medical facilities in advance and wear a mask for prompt evaluation.

Notable per-area rates include Ina 5.00, Iida 4.00, and Matsumoto City 3.00. Infectious gastroenteritis (norovirus and others) rose to 6.89 per sentinel, up 0.46, with Iida 15.00, Matsumoto 11.50, Matsumoto City 9.67. COVID-19 declined to 1.14 per sentinel, down 1.04, with Ueda 2.20, Suwa 1.60, Nagano City 1.44. Measles outbreaks continue; officials advise vaccination and caution during the Golden Week travel and post-return health checks. One elementary school closed for a grade, two for classes.

articles.headlineTranslated: Second measles case this year in Okinawa; man in his 30s infected, with overseas travel history.
articles.summary: Measles case in Okinawa: Okinawa Prefecture reports its second measles patient of the year. A man in his 30s from the Southern Health Center area developed fever and fatigue on the 24th after travel from Malaysia to Singapore, then returned to Okinawa. He arrived at Naha Airport's international arrivals between 8:35 and 9:00 on the 26th and took a taxi around 9:00. Laboratory confirmation of measles was made on the 28th by the prefectural Health and Environment Research Institute after genetic testing. He had contact with a measles patient in Malaysia and received measles vaccination on the 19th. As of the 29th he is recovering. Public health urges those with suspected measles symptoms to seek care after notifying clinics and to avoid public transport; measles virus can survive in air for up to two hours, and the places he visited are not currently infectious.

articles.summary: Tochigi Prefecture, Japan reports a measles surge with 16 cases as of April 29 in Heisei 26 (2014), the second-highest annual total since 2008's 46 cases. The outbreak is centered around the Tokyo metropolitan area and has spread mainly among people in their teens to 40s. Officials attribute the rise to overseas importation of the measles virus, with Tochigi’s year-to-date count rising sharply from last year’s single case and approaching the 2008 pace. Health authorities are urging vaccination for individuals with low measles antibody levels to curb transmission and prevent further spread.

Nationwide measles cases reached 197 by end-March (197 vs 58 Jan–Mar last year). Health guidance: seek prompt medical care for measles-like symptoms and avoid public transport to prevent spread; vaccination lowers risk.

articles.summary: Measles in Taiwan: a man in his 30s in central Taiwan tested positive after returning from Japan, marking the first imported measles case from Japan in seven years. He toured Nagoya in early April; fever and cough appeared on April 16 after the trip, with multiple medical visits. Rash emerged on April 20, and laboratory confirmation identified measles infection. The Taiwan CDC raised Japan’s travel alert to Level 1, advising adherence to routine preventive measures. Across 2026 to date, Taiwan has reported nine measles cases: two domestic transmissions and seven imported infections, with infection sources including Vietnam, Malaysia, the United States, India, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, and Japan.

articles.summary: Japan reports a measles outbreak with 299 cases confirmed as of April 15, 2026, and is on pace to exceed the 2019 total of 744. Despite WHO recognizing Japan as having eliminated endemic measles since 2015, current cases are believed imported, with school clusters reported and outbreaks associated with overseas sources. Data from the National Institute of Health Crisis Management show over 80% of patients are aged 15–49, with 20–39-year-olds comprising about half. Japan’s two-dose vaccination program began in 2006; those with only one dose may have insufficient immunity. Elimination targets require ≥95% vaccination for 1-year-olds and before entering elementary school; 2024 rates were 92% and 91%, respectively. Measles is airborne, and vaccination remains the only effective prevention, not routine hand hygiene or masks. The author recalls May 2019 when a rash during a meeting prompted immediate hospital contact during a measles concern.

articles.headlineTranslated: Editorial: We want to be vigilant and contain measles infections
articles.summary: Measles cases in Japan are rising domestically, with January-to-date totals exceeding 150—the highest since the 2020 pandemic—concentrated in Tokyo, Kanagawa, and Aichi. Although WHO classified Japan as measles-eliminated in 2015, importations have increased post-COVID as travel resumes, with returnees and visitors introducing the virus. Past decade peaked at 744 cases in 2019; 2020–2022 stayed under 10; 2025 reached 265; early 2026 saw clusters, including a February high-school outbreak in Aichi and infections among Tokyo restaurant workers. Incubation is 10–12 days; fever, upper-respiratory symptoms and conjunctivitis precede rash by 2–4 days, with fever recurrence for 3–4 days. Measles is highly contagious; infectious from day before rash to 3 days after fever, with nearly 100% attack rate in susceptibles. Prevention is vaccination: two-dose routine schedule (1-year and before elementary school) since 2006; many remain unvaccinated or have only one dose. Vigilance and clear public health messaging are urged.

articles.summary: Measles confirmed in a woman in her 30s in Kasuya District, Fukuoka Prefecture, marking the second measles case in the prefecture this year. The patient developed fever and headache on March 30, with rash and sore throat on March 31, and sought care on April 1 at a medical facility within the Kasuya Health Center jurisdiction. Genetic testing at the Fukuoka Prefectural Institute of Public Health and Environment confirmed measles. Vaccination history is unknown; no overseas travel history reported. Nationwide, measles cases totaled 265 in the previous year, and by February 22 this year had reached 152, indicating a faster spread. The prefecture urges people with fever and rash consistent with measles to contact a medical facility in advance and inform staff of suspected measles.
